issue.message: `usbReceiver` is missing `RECEIVER_EXPORTED` or `RECEIVER_NOT_EXPORTED` flag for unprotected broadcasts registered for null.USB_PERMISSION
issue.summary: Missing `registerReceiver()` exported flag
issue.explanation:
In Android U, all receivers registering for non-system broadcasts are required to include a flag indicating the receiver's exported state. Apps registering for non-system broadcasts should use the `ContextCompat#registerReceiver` APIs with flags set to either `RECEIVER_EXPORTED` or `RECEIVER_NOT_EXPORTED`.
If you are not expecting broadcasts from other apps on the device, register your receiver with `RECEIVER_NOT_EXPORTED` to protect your receiver on all platform releases.

issue.message: Exported service does not require permission
issue.summary: Exported service does not require permission
issue.explanation: Exported services (services which either set `exported=true` or contain an intent-filter and do not specify `exported=false`) should define a permission that an entity must have in order to launch the service or bind to it. Without this, any application can use this service.

issue.message: Do not place Android context classes in static fields (static reference to `NativeEnginePlayer` which has field `context` pointing to `Context`); this is a memory leak
issue.summary: Static Field Leaks
issue.explanation:
A static field will leak contexts.
Non-static inner classes have an implicit reference to their outer class. If that outer class is for example a `Fragment` or `Activity`, then this reference means that the long-running handler/loader/task will hold a reference to the activity which prevents it from getting garbage collected.
Similarly, direct field references to activities and fragments from these longer running instances can cause leaks.
ViewModel classes should never point to Views or non-application Contexts.

issue.message: Prefer `mutableFloatStateOf` instead of `mutableStateOf`
issue.summary: `State<T>` will autobox values assigned to this state. Use a specialized state type instead.
issue.explanation: Calling `mutableStateOf<T>()` when `T` is either backed by a primitive type on the JVM or is a value class results in a state implementation that requires all state values to be boxed. This usually causes an additional allocation for each state write, and adds some additional work to auto-unbox values when reading the value of the state. Instead, prefer to use a specialized primitive state implementation for `Int`, `Long`, `Float`, and `Double` when the state does not need to track null values and does not override the default `SnapshotMutationPolicy`. See `mutableIntStateOf()`, `mutableLongStateOf()`, `mutableFloatStateOf()`, and `mutableDoubleStateOf()` for more information.

issue.message: Should explicitly set `android:icon`, there is no default
issue.summary: Missing application icon
issue.explanation: You should set an icon for the application as whole because there is no default. This attribute must be set as a reference to a drawable resource containing the image (for example `@drawable/icon`).
